allow.reason: Its only parent-taking export resolves an external link through the vault and the metadata cache, which the catalogue stub deliberately refuses. Cell appearance is covered by card-field-renderer and number-display-renderer instead.

Every export resolves notes, tags or links through the vault. A fixture deep enough to render one would be a second implementation of file resolution, which is how the screenshot harness already went wrong.
Delegates to Obsidian's MarkdownRenderer, which has no standalone build. A story could only demonstrate the stub, not the rendering anyone cares about.
Icons may be backed by vault files, so rendering one outside Obsidian shows the fallback path rather than what ships.
A relation value is defined by the notes it points at; without the vault there is nothing to render but an empty shell.

Needs a full ViewConfig including schema, computed fields and grouping state. The fixture would be larger than the component and would drift from the real config shape, which makes it worse than no story.
Same ViewConfig dependency as the group label, plus per-group visible-count state that only the row pipeline produces.
Opens a dropdown from DatabaseView's active schema and bulk-edit transaction; a standalone frame would have to recreate that caller state instead of exercising this module's surface.
Attaches keyboard navigation to a CalendarRenderer grid and moves focus among its live cells; a static story would replace the grid and focus model it is meant to exercise.
Mutates tabindex across renderer-owned card cells after layout; a standalone fixture cannot establish the board, gallery or list roving group that supplies its active index.
Captures and restores scroll positions from live database and embedded-host scrollers; a static story has no host viewport lifecycle to exercise.
Resolves a drop edge from a live DragEvent, target geometry and transaction state; a static story cannot produce the browser drag state this feedback reports.
The parent-taking export writes the browser's native title tooltip, which has no standalone painted surface; formatting is covered by its unit-level callers.
Installs Obsidian workspace hover events and previews vault files; the Storybook stub has no workspace, vault or hover-popover lifecycle to render.
Traps focus inside a live modal scope and restores the prior active element; a static story cannot supply the modal ownership and focus lifecycle it coordinates.
Builds a picker through the live popover positioner and closes it through Obsidian's document-level auto-close events; a standalone frame would only duplicate those host events.
Attaches selection gestures to renderer-owned table cells and resolves touch versus mouse state; a static story cannot supply the table selection model those handlers mutate.
Attaches title-cell taps to the live record-peek lifecycle and opens a vault-backed row panel; a static story cannot exercise that owner and its cleanup path.

Read mode is Obsidian's MarkdownRenderer, which has no standalone build — the stub declares it out of scope, so a story could only demonstrate the stub, exactly as for inline-markdown-renderer.ts. The half a story could show is covered instead by note-body-region.test.ts, which drives the swap, focus, debounce and flush against a fake DOM, and by the two panel-record-detail-sheet-body-* screenshot scenarios.

Its one export removes the previous view's root from a container and takes the board's layout class off it. There is nothing to draw — a story would have to render a view first just to watch it disappear. The contract is exercised by board-renderer-parity.test.ts, which mounts a real board and asserts the container is clean afterwards.

Exports structural predicates over an already-mounted sheet element (describeSheetGrammar and the seven SHEET_GRAMMAR_ELEMENTS), not a renderer with its own DOM to preview. A story would have nothing to draw; the contract is exercised by tools/live/sheet-grammar.mjs against the real mounted surfaces instead.
